citations.narrative:
In the new barn housing the tigers, lions and hybrids, the enclosures consisted of 12 foot 2x4 inch 6 gauge welded wire,
with double layer fencing between enclosures. The enclosure dividers aligned with the roof trusses, making it difficult for
an animal to move into the neighboring enclosures over 12 foot fences. However, along the front, there was a gap
between the 12 foot front of the enclosure and the roof of the barn that was between 3 and 4 feet, potentially enough
space to allow a motivated animal a route. The facility must be constructed of such material and of such strength as
appropriate for the animals involved, therefore additional measures along the front fence of the enclosures are needed to
ensure that the enclosures contain the animals.
This inspection was an announced new site approval inspection.
This site is not ready for approval to conduct activity covered under your current Animal Welfare Act License.
Conducting regulated activities at a non-approved site is a violation of the Animal Welfare Act.
Please contact your inspector to schedule your next new site approval inspection.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with facility representatives.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of new site inspections must be received within 21
days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
